turns.speaker: Skeptic
turns.style: cocky, upbeat, fast-paced YouTube Shorts banter with sarcastic punch
turns.text: Wait... T. rex versus Triceratops? <pff> That's not a fight — that's lunch.

turns.speaker: Paleontologist
turns.style: warm, amused, deadpan delivery with crisp pause and emphasis on HEALED
turns.text: Yeah... <short pause> you'd think so. Except we found a Triceratops horn with T. rex bite marks — and the bone HEALED.

turns.speaker: Skeptic
turns.style: startled, energetic, rising incredulous pitch, brisk pace
turns.text: <gasp> Wait, what?! It survived a twelve-meter T. rex?! That thing packed thirty-five thousand newtons of bone-crushing bite force!

turns.speaker: Paleontologist
turns.style: confident, authoritative, brisk storytelling pace shifting to dry amusement after the pause
turns.text: True. Sixty-six million years ago in Hell Creek, T. rex had the strongest land bite ever. <short pause> Problem is... Triceratops wasn't some panicked salad bar.

turns.speaker: Skeptic
turns.style: curious, leaning in, snappy conversational question
turns.text: Okay, how big are we talking?

turns.speaker: Paleontologist
turns.style: impressed, punchy buildup dropping into deadpan dry comedic timing on the last sentence
turns.text: Nearly nine meters long, up to twelve tons — and a third of its ENTIRE body was just skull. Solid bony frill, one-meter brow horns. <chuckle> Basically an angry tank... <short pause> with steak knives taped to the bumper.

turns.speaker: Skeptic
turns.text: Still! Just circle around and bite its neck!

turns.speaker: Paleontologist
turns.style: lowered voice, conspiratorial and intense, crisp clear articulation, dramatic intrigue
turns.text: You see... <short pause> that's the trap. In 2008, fossils proved these two brawled face-to-face. Triceratops's skull sat on a giant ball-and-socket neck joint — so it pivoted that three-meter shield fast enough to keep two horns aimed straight at T. rex's face.

turns.speaker: Skeptic
turns.style: wide-eyed realization turning urgent and genuinely curious
turns.text: So charging straight in meant getting stabbed first... <short pause> okay, then how did T. rex EVER win?!

turns.speaker: Paleontologist
turns.style: ominous and serious, shifting into dark dry humor on the jar-lid reveal
turns.text: Unhealed tooth scores deep on the neck joint tell the grim story. <short pause> To reach the massive neck muscles past that shield, T. rex grabbed the frill... <snicker> and literally popped the head off like a jar lid.

turns.speaker: Paleontologist
turns.style: calm, dry, punchy final mic-drop delivery with crisp pause before Hard
turns.text: In Hell Creek... <short pause> dinner fought back. Hard.
